body:
On the latest episode of 
Predictable
, we went deep into one of my favorite things in politics:
A revenge plot with a market attached.
Louisiana has a Senate primary coming up, and on the surface, yes, it is a political story. Bill Cassidy voted to convict Donald Trump after January 6th. Trump remembered. Louisiana changed its primary system. Trump endorsed Julia Letlow before she even officially announced. Subtle stuff.
But the real story is not “Trump wants revenge.” Everyone knows that.
The real story is this:
Are the markets pricing that revenge correctly?
That is where things get interesting.
The Cassidy Trapdoor
For years, Cassidy had something that helped protect him: Louisiana’s old jungle primary system. That meant crossover voters could help a more moderate Republican survive. Democrats, independents, anti-Trump Republicans, whoever. If you could build the right coalition, you had a path.
Then, Louisiana changed the rules.
Now, Cassidy has to survive something much closer to a normal Republican primary. Which is not exactly ideal when the most powerful man in Republican politics has decided your political career should be placed gently into a wood chipper.
Cassidy’s current market price?
Around 
2%
.
And honestly, that may not be wrong.
Where the Market Gets Interesting
Julia Letlow is the heavy favorite to win the primary. That makes sense. She has Trump’s endorsement, and we just watched what happened in Indiana when Republican candidates crossed Trump on redistricting.
Spoiler: It did not go great for them.
But here is the market that caught my eye:
Julia Letlow winning outright without a runoff.
That was sitting around 
9%
.
Now, a 9% position is not something you expect to hit most of the time. That is the point. You are supposed to lose those most of the time.
But what if you think the real number is closer to 20, 25, maybe even 30%? Now we are talking about value.
That is the kind of spot we look for on this show. Not “who do I like?” Not “what does the headline say?” Not “what would make me feel emotionally validated while watching cable news?”
The question is simple: 
Is the market wrong?
And if it is wrong, can we get there before everyone else notices?
The 10x Setup
If Letlow consolidates enough of the Trump vote, if Fleming fades, if voters decide they would rather end this thing Saturday than come back for a runoff, that 9% starts looking very interesting.
Still a long shot.
Still risky.
Still the kind of thing that can make you look very dumb for a few hours.
But that is also why the price exists.
The boring version of this race is Letlow and Fleming in a runoff. That is what the market expects. That may very well be what happens.
But the fun version?
The fun version is Trump’s endorsement turns this from a primary into a coronation, and the market was too slow to catch up.
Why This Is the Show
This is exactly why we built 
Predictable
.
Politics gives you the noise. Prediction markets give you the price.
The opportunity lives in the gap.
On this episode, we walked through the Cassidy story, the Louisiana rule change, the Trump revenge tour, the runoff math, and why a tiny-looking market position might actually be the most interesting part of the entire race.
And yes, we also got into why you should have more than one market app open, why small gains matter, and why chasing volume just to feel busy is a great way to light money on fire.
But the Louisiana market is the one to watch.
Because somewhere inside this weird little Saturday primary is a possible 10x trade.
The question is whether it is real.
And that is what we tried to figure out.
